precepts.text: They built the high places of Tophet in the valley of Hinnom to burn their sons and daughters in the fire, a thing the Most High commanded not, neither came it into His heart.
precepts.point: He burned incense in the valley of the son of Hinnom and burned his children in the fire, after the abominations of the heathen that the Most High cast out before the children of Israel. This was witchcraft and child sacrifice, the practice called Tophet, in the high places under every green tree.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 28: Ahaz Trusts Other Nations and Their Gods

precepts.why:
“For the children of Judah have done evil in my sight, saith the Lord”. “And they have built the high places of Tophet, which is in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire; which I commanded them not, neither came it into my heart.”

That is what Ahaz did. He “burnt incense in the valley of the son of Hinnom, and burnt his children in the fire, after the abominations of the heathen whom the Lord had cast out before the children of Israel.” This was witchcraft and child sacrifice, the practice called Tophet, in the high places “and under every green tree.”

Ahaz “did not that which was right in the sight of the Lord, like David his father”. He walked in the ways of the kings of Israel and “made also molten images for Baalim”, a thing the Most High commanded not, neither came it into his heart.

precepts.text: In the days of Ahaz, Syria and Ephraim came up against Jerusalem but could not prevail; the Most High foretold that within threescore and five years Ephraim would be broken.
precepts.point: Zichri, a mighty man of Ephraim, slew the king's son, the governor of the house, and the man next to the king. The children of Israel carried away captive of their brethren two hundred thousand women, sons, and daughters, and much spoil, and brought it to Samaria. This was brother against brother, one nation of Israel captiving the other.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 28: Ahaz Trusts Other Nations and Their Gods

precepts.why:
It was “in the days of Ahaz” that “Rezin the king of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up toward Jerusalem to war against it, but could not prevail against it.” It was told the house of David, “Syria is confederate with Ephraim”, and the heart of Ahaz and his people was moved “as the trees of the wood are moved with the wind.”

The Most High sent Isaiah to tell Ahaz, “Take heed, and be quiet; fear not”, for the evil counsel of Syria and Ephraim “shall not stand, neither shall it come to pass.” He foretold that “within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people.” And he warned, “If ye will not believe, surely ye shall not be established.”

These are the same two kings in Chronicles. Because Judah “had forsaken the Lord God of their fathers”, the Most High delivered Ahaz “into the hand of the king of Syria”, who carried captives to Damascus, and “into the hand of the king of Israel”. “Pekah the son of Remaliah slew in Judah an hundred and twenty thousand in one day, which were all valiant men”. Zichri, “a mighty man of Ephraim”, slew the king’s son, the governor of the house and the man next to the king, and “the children of Israel carried away captive of their brethren two hundred thousand” to Samaria. This was brother against brother, one nation of Israel captiving the other.

precepts.text: If your brother waxes poor and is sold to you, you shall not make him serve as a bondservant, but as a hired servant, and he shall go free in the year of jubilee.
precepts.point: The men named by name took the captives, clothed all that were naked among them, shod them, gave them to eat and drink, anointed them, carried the feeble on asses, and brought them to Jericho, the city of palm trees, to their brethren, then returned to Samaria. Even in the middle of the division, these men feared the Most High and would not treat their brethren as slaves.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 28: Ahaz Trusts Other Nations and Their Gods

precepts.why:
The law said, “if thy brother that dwelleth by thee be waxen poor, and be sold unto thee; thou shalt not compel him to serve as a bondservant: But as an hired servant, and as a sojourner, he shall be with thee, and shall serve thee unto the year of jubile”. Then “shall he depart from thee, both he and his children with him, and shall return unto his own family”. A brother was never to be made a bondservant.

That is why Oded rebuked the host that came to Samaria. The Most High had delivered Judah into their hand because of his wrath, but they had “slain them in a rage that reacheth up unto heaven”, and now they purposed “to keep under the children of Judah and Jerusalem for bondmen and bondwomen unto you”. That is against the law, and it added to their own sins: “are there not with you, even with you, sins against the Lord your God?”

Certain heads of the children of Ephraim stood up too: “we have offended against the Lord already, ye intend to add more to our sins and to our trespass”. So the armed men left the captives and the spoil, and the men named by name clothed the naked, shod them, gave them “to eat and to drink, and anointed them, and carried all the feeble of them upon asses, and brought them to Jericho, the city of palm trees, to their brethren”. Even in the middle of the division, these men feared the Most High and would not treat their brethren as slaves.

precepts.text: The Most High will assemble the outcasts of Israel and gather the dispersed of Judah; then Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim.
precepts.point: Ahaz slept with his fathers and they buried him in the city, in Jerusalem, but not in the sepulchres of the kings of Israel, and Hezekiah his son reigned in his stead. The Most High is the only one who can bring the people out of their condition, then and now.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 28: Ahaz Trusts Other Nations and Their Gods

precepts.why:
The Most High “shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” Then “The envy also of Ephraim shall depart”, and “Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim.”

Ahaz ran the other way: “in the time of his distress did he trespass yet more against the Lord”. He sacrificed to the gods of Damascus that smote him, saying, “Because the gods of the kings of Syria help them, therefore will I sacrifice to them, that they may help me. But they were the ruin of him, and of all Israel.” He cut in pieces “the vessels of the house of God, and shut up the doors of the house of the Lord, and he made him altars in every corner of Jerusalem.”

That is the pattern of running to a nation that cannot save, the same spirit that trusts in the systems of the world instead of the Most High. The Most High is the only one who can bring the people out of their condition, then and now: it is he who assembles the outcasts, gathers the dispersed, and ends the envy between Ephraim and Judah.
